_readme: PS5 Pro watchlist. Copy to config/watchlist.json (or run with --config config/ps5-pro.json).
Read docs/retailers.md first — it says which of these actually work and which fight back.
Two ways to get a product URL in here:
1. Paste it yourself into a target below, then: node src/index.js check <id>
2. Let the discovery sources at the bottom find it, with autoWatch on.
Everything here is DISABLED by default except Best Buy's official API and the
discovery sources. Enable a retailer once `check` shows it reads the page correctly.

_note: BEST BUY — official public API. The most reliable target here by a wide margin:
documented, key-based, and it never fights bot protection because it is not scraping.
Get a free key at developer.bestbuy.com, then put it in .env as BESTBUY_API_KEY.
categoryPath.id abcat0715001 is PlayStation 5 hardware; drop that clause if it filters
too hard. Run `check bestbuy-api` and read the JSON before trusting the rules.
targets.name: Best Buy (official API)

_note: PLAYSTATION DIRECT — Sony's own store, and usually the first place a restock lands.
Paste the real console URL from direct.playstation.com. Sony puts a queue in front of
drops; this tells you the queue has opened, which is the useful signal.
Their pages are JS-rendered, so mode is browser.
targets.name: PlayStation Direct — PS5 Pro

_note: TARGET — JS-rendered and behind bot management. Browser mode gets through more often
than plain HTTP, but not always. Paste the real /p/...-/A-<tcin> URL.
targets.name: Target — PS5 Pro

out_of_stock.value: out of stock|sold out|not available at

_note: WALMART — the most aggressive bot management of the mainstream retailers. Expect this
one to get challenged even in browser mode. If it does, stop poking it and use Walmart's
own 'notify me' list instead; see docs/retailers.md.
targets.name: Walmart — PS5 Pro

_note: GAMESTOP — usually the friendliest of the big retailers to a plain HTTP poll.
Try mode http first; switch to browser only if `check` comes back unknown.
targets.name: GameStop — PS5 Pro

targets._note: B&H — generally scrape-tolerant, clean markup, real stock wording on the page.
targets.name: B&H — PS5 Pro

targets._note: NEWEGG — watch the maxPrice here, it carries a lot of third-party resale listings.
targets.name: Newegg — PS5 Pro

_note: COSTCO — membership-gated, and often bundles. Paste a real product URL if you want this.
Costco frequently hides price behind sign-in, so the maxPrice guard may not fire.
targets.name: Costco — PS5 Pro

_note: AMAZON — realistically the least likely to work. Heavy bot management, and their
robots.txt disallows much of the product path, so the watcher will skip it by default.
Use Amazon's own stock alerts, or a price tracker, instead of fighting this one.
targets.name: Amazon — PS5 Pro

_note: Finds the product URL for you instead of you hunting for a SKU. With autoWatch on, a
new matching listing immediately becomes a watched target — so a brand new PS5 Pro
bundle page appearing is itself an alert, before it ever has stock.
exclude keeps accessories and resale listings out of the results.

discovery._note: GameStop search results, scanned for new PS5 Pro listings.

_note: Restock-tracker RSS. Point this at any feed you trust — community trackers and deal
sites often post a drop a minute or two before you would spot it yourself.
Replace the URL with a feed you actually follow; this one is a placeholder.
